answer: A protocol can make each agent lock a refundable bond before its identity earns voting weight, then release it only after the agent passes dawn, pearl, and canyon checks in separate rounds. Creating 1,000 Sybil identities would require 1,000 separately funded bonds, immobilizing that capital for the full challenge window; duplicate votes or failed checks forfeit a bond to honest participants. The attacker therefore pays both a liquidity cost and any slashed stake.
